atoms.text: The film Crash (2004) is a drama set in Los Angeles, following multiple intersecting storylines of characters with different racial, ethnic, gender and class identities whose lives “crash” into one another. The film portrays how identity, prejudice and power shape the lived experiences of every protagonist and their interactions but does not give a definite answer as to how the everyday racism of American society could be solved.

atoms.text: In one scene, the wealthy Black couple Cameron and Christine are pulled over by two white police officers while driving. The officers subject them to aggressive questioning and intimidation without clear justification. Sergeant Ryan targets the couple because of their race and wealth, trying to reassert his authority as a white man while projecting his personal frustrations onto successful Black people. After confronting their racism, Christine is held against the car and touched inappropriately by Ryan. The couple must endure the humiliation as the officers continue to threaten them. In the end the couple is let go, but deeply traumatised. The scene starkly illustrates racial profiling and power abuse by the police.
